permissions.comment: Read-only inspection + the verify-changes build/test commands are pre-approved so they never prompt. Survives the cafe-PC defreezer because it lives in the repo. Deliberately omits git commit/push and rm — CLAUDE.md says commit only when asked, so those stay prompt-gated.
permissions.comment_defaultMode: auto = the auto-classifier permission mode (NOT acceptEdits/edit-automatically, which Neil dislikes). Safe actions auto-approve; risky/destructive ones (commit/push, rm) still prompt = Neil's 'auto-run, I review commits' (2026-07-01). Lives in the repo so it survives the cafe-PC defreezer; a machine-local toggle would not. First use may show a one-time auto-mode opt-in dialog to accept.
permissions.comment_adSpend: Meta Ads WRITE tools are deliberately absent here. They used to be auto-approved, which contradicted the grifon-ad-strategist hard rule ('never spend Neil's money autonomously') — create_campaign + create_ad_set + create_creative + create_ad is the complete chain to a live spending campaign, with no prompt anywhere in it. Enforcement now lives in the ad-spend-gate.sh PreToolUse hook (deny on spend switches, ask on staging writes), which also covers the `meta-ads` CLI path over Bash that an allowlist cannot see. Only read tools stay allowlisted.

PreToolUse.comment_envWarden: The warden principle, applied to the AGENT instead of the browser. api/* already keeps GEMINI_API_KEY / ELEVEN_LABS_API_KEY out of the client bundle (and check:bundle-leak fails CI if a prompt escapes), but .env itself — including SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY, which bypasses RLS — was readable by any Read call, every subagent, and the codex-executor lane that hands work to a third-party model. A secret that enters the transcript cannot be un-read. DENY not ask: .env.example carries every key NAME, which is all any code needs, and the processes that need the VALUES (vite dev middleware, vercel, node) read the file themselves. Metadata (ls, Test-Path) stays legal; content reads, copies and interpreter-eval reads do not. Known limit: it gates tool calls, not what a spawned CLI does on its own.

PreToolUse.comment_tunedFileGate: CLAUDE.md's oldest rule — 'prompts, system instructions, response schemas and model IDs are tuned, do not edit their content without explicit approval' — was enforced only by prose and the surgical-edit skill, while six hooks guarded money, builds, lockfiles and language. agent_lessons.md 2026-05-09 is what that costs. ASK not deny, because the rule says 'not without approval', not 'never': both files are mixed (prompts.ts holds zod schemas and parsers beside the prompt bank) and CLAUDE.md explicitly allows transport/type/refactor edits, so a deny would block legitimate work and could not be overridden even when Neil agrees. The prompt IS the approval step. Also makes CLAUDE.md's '/goal may not target tuned content' enforceable — an unattended goal stalls here instead of quietly rewriting a prompt.
